summary: The root نأي primarily signifies being or going far away, remote, or distant. It implies separation, removal, or withdrawal from something or someone.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: نَأَى بِهِ [ He, or it, removed him; put or placed him at a distance, away, or far away. ] (S, art. طرح.) نَأَى He shrank from a thing: see an ex. in a verse cited voce دَفٌّ.
أَنْآهُ: see آنَاهُ in art. انى.
اِسْتَنْأَى: i. q. اِسْتَنَاءَ q. v. in art. نوأ.
نُؤْىٌ A trench dug round a tent, (S, K,) or a barrier [ raised ] around it, (T, IB, TA,) to prevent the rain-water from entering it, (S,) or keep off a torrent. (K.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
